checksums.name: none_identified
checksums.formula_detail: No checksum/magic routine in 35 decompiled functions or 3 save-related functions; no sum/xor/crc loop feeding FUN_08036944/FUN_08036880. Candidate sums tested in Python (see verified_on_samples) do not consistently explain any stored byte across all 4 hypothesized slots: slot0 sum8_excl_byte7=0x08 equals byte14 only coincidentally (slots1-3 sum_excl=0x00 vs byte14=0x00 trivially zero, byte7=0x01 unexplained).

verified_on_samples.computed_hex: sum8=0x07 sum16le=0xff08 xor8=0xf5 crc32=0xbe9dd84f; per-slot sum8=04,01,01,01

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 driver (generic DMA): param1->DMA SAD 0x040000D4, param2->DAD 0x040000D8, param3|0x80000000 ->CNT 0x040000DC, polls CNT bit31/busy, saves/restores interrupt state via DAT ptrs. Used both RAM->0x0D000000 and 0x0D000000->RAM. CONFIRMED_STATIC from save_related_functions.c:809-833.

EEPROM Read: param1=block addr (<desc[+4]), param2=dest RAM (8B). Builds addr bitstream MSB-first per desc[+8] addr bits, sends '11' header (two 1 halfwords) via FUN_08036800(buf,0x0D000000,addrBits+3), reads 0x44=68 halfwords (64 data+4 dummy) via FUN_08036800(0x0D000000,buf,0x44), unpacks 64 bits MSB-first into 4x u16le at dest+6,4,2,0. No callers in callgraph.json (truncated/indirect).

EEPROM Write: param1=block addr, param2=src RAM (4x u16=8B), param3=wait/poll flag. Packs 64 data bits + addr bits MSB-first, header 0,1 ('10' write), DMA len addrBits+0x43 to 0x0D000000, then polls 0x0D000000 bit0 ready with timer DAT_08036a30 timeout 0x88 ticks (wrap 0xe4). No callers in callgraph.json.

fields.name: eeprom_blank_fill
fields.update_mechanism: cap-00 is erased/uninitialized EEPROM (reads 0xFF); cap-01 shows game/emulator initialized to 0x00 - writer of bulk zero unknown (could be 64x FUN_08036944 block writes by untraced caller).
fields.evidence: Python sha256 cap00=9f56cda75fefeab9... all-FF verified; cap01=7eb73968d59482c2... 507x 0x00.

fields.name: slot0_byte7_flags_hypothesis
fields.update_mechanism: Written as part of EEPROM block 0 (addr 0, bytes0-7) via FUN_08036944 8B write; in-RAM updater unknown (no caller traced). Bits 11111100: six high bits set - progress/valid flags hypothesis only.
fields.evidence: .sav offset7=0xFC in cap01; driver writes in 8B blocks so offset7 is last byte of block0. No field-specific writer in decompiled.c.

fields.name: slot0_byte14
fields.update_mechanism: Part of EEPROM block1 (bytes8-15) 8B write; updater unknown. Coincidentally equals slot0 sum8 excluding byte7 (0x08) - not proven checksum (see checksums).
fields.evidence: .sav offset14=0x08 cap01; Python slot0 sum_excl7=0x08 but slots1-3 do not corroborate a checksum at +14 (all zero).

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If valid/progress flags: save rejected/reinitialized or levels lock/unlock. No checksum repair known (none identified); if rejected, checksum hypothesis gains support.
Distinguishes counter/flag vs checksum-byte: gameplay value change vs save-invalid.
If slot1 valid flag: slot appears/disappears in load UI; if global flag replicated, all slots change behavior.

0xFF: blank-boot/reinit (PACKET cold-reload says cap-01 preserved, not reverted). All-zero: tests whether zero is accepted as valid empty save or reinitialized to cap-01 pattern (0xFC/0x08/0x01s rewritten).
If no effect and no rejection, block is padding/unused at this progress state.

open_questions: Ultimate callers of FUN_08036880/FUN_08036944 absent from trace-guided set (callgraph callers=[]) - in-RAM save struct address (EWRAM/IWRAM), slot selection, and serialization order unknown.
Is geometry 4x128B slots, 1 global 512B image, or 64 independent 8B blocks? Repeated +7 byte supports 128B stride but n=1 progressed sample cannot prove it.
No magic or checksum identified - either none exists (flags only), or serializer/checksum caller not decompiled. Need progressed saves with more nonzero bytes.
EEPROM descriptor values (desc+4 capacity, desc+8 address bits) not resolved from DAT constants in decompilation - 6-bit address inferred from 512B size, not read from ROM data.
Meaning of 0xFC at 0x07 and 0x08 at 0x0E: progress flags, counters, language/settings, or bit-packed data? Bit order of emulator .sav vs on-wire EEPROM bitstream assumed logical-byte order.
